texts.facts: The present claim arises out of a detailed accident report (Dar), filed by the police in terms of the provision of Motor Vehicle Act in which claimant Parmeshvari Dayal sustained injuries. Brief facts of the case are that on 20.06.2022 at about 11.20 PM, claimant who was working as a delivery boy, left for D-210, Defence Colony on his motorcycle bearing no.DL-6SBD-9852. At around 11.25 pm, when he reached near Govt. Boys Sr. Sec. school, Varun Marg, Defence Colony, a car bearing no. DL-3CBA-4081 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) driven in rash and negligent manner hit his motorcycle, due to which he fell down. Due to the impact, even the bumper of said car fell apart. As a result, petitioner sustained injuries on his head and right hip. He was shifted to Safdarjung hospital for treatment. 3. An FIR no.0125/2022 u/s 279/338 IPC was registered against the driver of the offending vehicle. After investigation, chargesheet was filed before concerned criminal court against the driver of the offending vehicle(Respondent no.1) while present DAR was filed before this Tribunal. 4. Respondent no.1 and 2 filed their reply submitting that DAR is bad for mis-joinder of parties as accident did not take place due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle. MACT NO.527/24 Parmeshvari Dayal v. Virendra Singh P.No. 2 Of 19 BK It is pleaded that driver of offending vehicle was having valid driving licence at the time of accident and offending vehicle was also duly insured on the date of accident. Respondent no.3/insurance company filed legal offer for Rs.2,14,073/- which was declined by the petitioner. 5. Vide order dated 20.08.2024, following issues were framed. 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 20.06.2022 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. DL-3CBA-4081 being driven by R1, owned by R2 and insured with R3? OPP 2. Whether the injured is entitled to compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom? OPP. 3. Relief. 6. Evidence was recorded through learned Local Commissioner. To prove his claim, petitioner Parmeshvari Dayal led his evidence by examining himself as PW-1 by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He reiterated the version as of the DAR. He deposed that he was working as delivery boy and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m. He spent Rs.75,000/- on attendant, special diet, treatment and Rs.50,000/- on conveyance and medical bills. He suffered 26% permanent disability in relation to right lower limb. He relied upon his Aadhar card as Ex.PW-1/1, PAN card as Ex.PW-1/2, MLC as Ex.PW-1/3 & Discharge summary as Ex.PW-1/4, treatment records and OPD cards as Ex.PW-1/5, bank statement as Ex.PW-1/6(colly), Dunzo job ID card as Ex.PW-1/7, medical bills of Rs.36,018/- as Ex.PW-1/8(colly), Disability certificate as Ex.PW-1/9, DAR as Ex.PW-1/10, driving MACT NO.527/24 Parmeshvari Dayal v. Virendra Singh P.No. 3 Of 19 BK licence as Ex.Ex.PW-1/11. He was Parameshvari Dayal(Dar) vs Virendra Singh (125/22 Dfc) on 19 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158471742/ 2 cross-examined by Ld.counsel for Respondents. No evidence has been led on behalf of the respondents. 7. Final arguments in details were addressed on behalf of the claimant/injured and the insurance company. 9. In the instant case, petitioner/injured Parmeshvari Dayal have examined himself to prove the factum as well as manner of accident. In his cross-examination, victim denied the suggestion that he was driving rashly and negligently. In fact, while being cross-examined by Respondent no.1 and 2, no suggestion MACT NO.527/24 Parmeshvari Dayal v. Virendra Singh P.No. 4 Of 19 BK denying the occurrence of accident has been put and none of the respondents have stepped into the witness box to prove their assertion that it was petitoner who was at fault. 10. Further, after investigating even the police has filed a chargesheet against Respondent no.1 which shows that the accident was reported without any inordinate delay. Accordingly, issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioners and against the respondents. As regards liability, insurance company had filed a legal offer, thus not raising any statutory defence. No breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy has been pleaded. As such, Respondent no.3 is liable to indemnify the respondents and MACT NO.527/24 Parmeshvari Dayal v. Virendra Singh P.No. 5 Of 19 BK compensate the petitioner.
texts.arguments: . Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & Ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of charge sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 13. As regards the quantum of compensation, this court is governed by the law laid down by Hon'le Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680. The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured MACT NO.527/24 Parmeshvari Dayal v. Virendra Singh P.No. 6 Of 19 BK would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii) (a) and (iv). 14.6. Observation of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rajkumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. is quoted hereunder: Parmeshvari Dayal v. Virendra Singh P.No. 8 Of 19 BK compensation under the head of `loss of future earnings', if the claimant continues in government service, though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities as a consequence of losing his hand. In turn, the State Bank of India, Saket Courts Branch shall receive the deposited sum and capture the above information and furnish a MACT NO.527/24 Parmeshvari Dayal v. Virendra Singh P.No. 13 Of 19 BK statement of account on a daily basis to the Nazir of this Tribunal to reconcile the deposits of compensation and the respective MCOPs towards which such deposits are made. 26. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: " ......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". In the case of illiterate claimants, the Tribunal is allowed to consider the request for lumpsum payment for effecting purchase of any movable property such as agricultural implements, rickshaws etc. to earn a living. In the case of semi-illiterate claimants, the MACT NO.527/24 Parmeshvari Dayal v. Virendra Singh P.No. 15 Of 19 BK Tribunal should ordinarily invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit. But if the Tribunal is satisfied for reasons to be stated in writing that the whole or part of the amount is required for expanding an existing business or for purchasing some property for earning a livelihood, the Tribunal can release the whole or part of the amount of compensation to the claimant provided the Tribunal will ensure that the amount is invested for the purpose for which it is demanded and paid. appreciating the distinction drawn by this Court in the case of minors, illiterate claimants and widows MACT NO.527/24 Parmeshvari Dayal v. Virendra Singh P.No. 16 Of 19 BK and in the case of semiliterate and literate persons.
